entries.subject: Bulge
entries.finding: Salo et al. (2015), S4G Pipeline 4, table 7, NGC4548, model _bdbarf: a Sérsic bulge (10.5% of the light, magnitude 12.0, half-light radius 5.7″ = 0.45 kpc, n = 2.56, axis ratio 0.869, PA 115.78°) and an exponential disc (78.0% of the light, scale length 55.9″ = 4.39 kpc, axis ratio 0.777, PA 149.2°, face-on central surface brightness 20.559, 20.285 as projected on the sky) and a Ferrers bar (11.4% of the light, radius 62.25″ = 4.89 kpc, axis ratio 0.458, PA 63.77°, central surface brightness 20.084 on the sky). Used as published; the half-light surface brightness the bake needs, 18.784 mag per square arcsecond, follows from the bulge's magnitude, radius, index and axis ratio. At the disc's 38.3° the bulge's axis ratio is one an oblate spheroid in the disc plane can show (intrinsic 0.60).
